<issue>Issue Title: [BUG] Condition needs to be modified to check if self.llm is either of LLM or BaseLLM classes
Description:
https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/blob/a0fcc0c8d19d212e5b24cbcc3563ddcbb36d88cd/src/crewai/lite_agent.py#L212
Looks like the above condition is supposed to check if `self.llm` is an instance of either `BaseLLM` or `LLM`
I found this issue when I tried to used the guardrails with the `CustomLLM` class that is inherited from `BaseLLM`.
Requesting to please check this condition and update accordingly.
Thanks
</issue>

Analysis of the collected context:

1. The code snippet from src/crewai/lite_agent.py around line 212 shows a method setup_llm inside the LiteAgent class. This method assigns self.llm the output of create_llm(self.llm), and then checks if self.llm is an instance of LLM. If not, it raises a ValueError.

2. The bug description says that this condition should check if self.llm is an instance of either BaseLLM or LLM. This is important because custom LLM implementations inherit from BaseLLM and the current check only accepts LLM instances, so any subclasses like CustomLLM that inherit from BaseLLM but are not of type LLM will fail the condition.

3. The intended behavior based on the issue is that the isinstance check on self.llm in setup_llm should verify that self.llm is either an instance of BaseLLM or LLM to support subclasses of BaseLLM.

4. Additional context was searched by retrieving the classes BaseLLM and LLM. BaseLLM is an abstract base class for LLMs, located in src/crewai/llms/base_llm.py. LLM is a concrete implementation located in src/crewai/llm.py, and it inherits from BaseLLM.

In summary, the current bug lies in the setup_llm method in LiteAgent where it only allows self.llm to be an instance of LLM, but according to the issue, it should accept any instance that is a subclass or instance of BaseLLM (including LLM itself).

No other context is needed for the fix because the problem is localized to the condition on line 212 in setup_llm method of LiteAgent. We already know the relevant classes to check against.

Next step could be to look for the create_llm function definition or usage to ensure we understand what it does, but since the issue is only about modifying the isinstance condition, we presumably have enough to draft a fix.
